# S1 fictional acceptance fixtures

`acceptance.json` is shared by native Rust and renderer TypeScript tests. It is not a production catalog or application asset. All species/form identities, moves, resources, targets and outcomes are original fictional examples. Repeated hexadecimal digests only distinguish invented provenance versions.

The nine cases cover evolution-first preparation, use now with optional investment, power-up-first preparation, missing identity/moves/mechanics, zero versus unknown budgets, protection conflict, stale input/version context with an old action report, and a required untagged move-change action. Decimal strings above JavaScript's safe-integer range check lossless transport. Target numbers use fictional fold units and assert no Pokémon GO fact.

Rust tests validate structure and internal consistency, not strategic accuracy. Renderer tests read the same JSON through test-only exact field maps tied to the TypeScript DTO keys; no live parser, command, UI, planner, persistence or model consumes these fixtures.
